summary: Explains how to use `ansible-galaxy collection download` to fetch collections and their dependencies for offline installation. Downloads go to `./collections` by default along with a generated `requirements.yml`, and collections can be given by name, version, requirements file, or source directory.
questions: How do I download a collection so I can install it on a server with no internet access?
How can I grab a specific version of a collection for an air-gapped install?
Can I download every collection listed in my requirements.yml in one go?
Where does ansible-galaxy collection download put the files by default?
If I point collection download at a tarball URL, does it use that tarball or re-download?
Can I download a collection from a local source directory or git repo?

answer_card.title: Download collections for an offline install
answer_card.answer_md:
Run `ansible-galaxy collection download` on an internet-connected host. It fetches the collections plus their dependencies into `./collections` and writes a `requirements.yml` you can use on the offline host.

```bash
# one collection (and deps)
ansible-galaxy collection download my_namespace.my_collection
# pinned version
ansible-galaxy collection download my_namespace.my_collection:1.0.0
# everything in a requirements file
ansible-galaxy collection download -r requirements.yml
# from a source dir or git repo (built from galaxy.yml)
ansible-galaxy collection download /path/to/collection
ansible-galaxy collection download git+file:///path/to/collection/.git
```

Collections are sourced from your configured Galaxy server; even a collection given by tarball URL or path is downloaded again from that server.
